overwriteSwap.title: Swap in the read's table
overwriteSwap.description: When an overwrite's read ends, put the table the read was written to in the target's place, by renaming it, if the target then differs in nothing but its OID: the table gets the target's columns' defaults and NOT NULL, constraints, indexes, owner, privileges, comments and storage parameters. A target with anything else, such as a view on it, triggers, foreign keys or a publication, or that the user doesn't own, has the rows copied in. The swap holds an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on the target while it renames, waiting up to 5 seconds for it, and copies the rows in if the lock doesn't come; it isn't MVCC-safe: a transaction whose snapshot is older, and that reads the table first after the swap, sees only the read's rows that were applied when its snapshot was taken. false copies the rows in always, so the table keeps its OID.

overwriteTruncate.title: Truncate before copying in
overwriteTruncate.description: When an overwrite copies the read's rows into the target, empty it with TRUNCATE rather than DELETE: no WAL for each old row, and no dead rows. TRUNCATE holds an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on the table, which blocks its readers until the copy commits, and isn't MVCC-safe: a transaction whose snapshot is older sees the table empty. It waits up to 5 seconds for the lock, and deletes the rows if the lock doesn't come or a foreign key refers to the table. Needs the TRUNCATE privilege.

tlsCa.description: PEM certificates of the authorities that sign the server's certificate, given in place of the dsn's sslrootcert file. The server's certificate must chain to them under every sslmode that uses TLS, and also name the dsn's host under verify-full. Setting it makes TLS required: sslmode=disable or allow is refused, and prefer doesn't fall back to a plaintext connection.
tlsCa.title: CA certificates

tlsCert.description: A PEM client certificate, in place of the dsn's sslcert file, for a server that asks for one, such as with the cert authentication method or clientcert=verify-full. Needs tlsKey, and makes TLS required as tlsCa does.
tlsCert.title: Client certificate

tlsKey.description: The client certificate's private key, PEM, unencrypted, in place of the dsn's sslkey file.
tlsKey.title: Client key
